brief: Morning flow note from GS flagging NFP as benign (softer payrolls, higher unemployment, better participation), easing the immediate Fed path and extending last week's curve steepening, though GS says it wasn't a genuine bull steepener since the back end had already sold off; a steeper curve can still coexist with a supportive Fed path if the market keeps believing in strong nominal growth. Oil tankers were hit again but crude keeps exiting the Gulf, capping the extreme tail risk; oil is slightly lower. In Europe, Spain's snap-election risk and France's fiscal/political anxiety (OAT/Bund spread widening) are hitting EUR, with this week's question being whether alternative French candidates can show a credible fiscal path. Brazil's first-round result (Bolsonaro 47.0%, Lula 45.2%) is substantially better than expected, so GS expects a rally and front-loaded pricing of the second round, supportive for BRL and Brazilian risk assets. On positioning: sentiment is depressed, funds de-risked aggressively and net exposure sits near 5-year lows even as the Nasdaq breaks out while over half the Russell sits 20% off highs; GS reads this extremely light positioning as a setup for the market to bleed higher, with earnings season expected to be strong, while flagging French/European sovereign risk and energy as the key risks to that view.
